text:
anya: FYI starting intake for new community model weights + tokenizer (repo: github.com/thirdparty/fast-llm, tag v0.9). posting proposed minimal ingest checks so we can move to registry and run quant experiments.

mike: can you paste the source URLs? also do we have a signed release?

anya: s3://ext-uploads/fast-llm/v0.9/weights.zip and s3://ext-uploads/fast-llm/v0.9/tokenizer.tar.gz. there is a RELEASES.md that claims sha256 hashes but no GPG sig.

sara: ok we should treat as untrusted until we verify. proposed quick checklist for "mini" ingest (short, actionable):
- verify S3 object checksum matches RELEASES.md (sha256)
- download or fetch copy into staging bucket with object lock metadata
- extract and run tokenizer unit tests (basic tokenize/detokenize +/- sample prompts)
- run small sample generation with weights (1-2 prompts, 64 tokens) to detect gross failure modes
- generate model-card metadata: architecture, vocab_size, tokenizer_class, license, source_url, release_tag, contact
- sign the manifest (sigstore or GPG) and push manifest to model-registry (s3://redwood-model-registry/public/fast-llm/v0.9/)

mike: sounds good. add KMS-wrapping for the staged copy? we should KMS-encrypt copied object and set lifecycle to move to infrequent after 30d.

anya: yes, staging bucket uses kms key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111:alias/redwood-ingest. lifecycle 30d->GLACIER is separate infra ticket.

david: who will run the initial quantization sweep? i'll take int8 and int4 with the usual per-layer outlier clamp. will need a clean model build in dedicated test pool.

anya: david you're on quant sweep. mike do checksum + GPG attempt (if no upstream sig we create local manifest and sig via sigstore). sara do tokenizer sanity + model-card draft. i'll do registry entry + provenance fields.

mike: starting checksum now, command I ran:
```bash
aws s3 cp s3://ext-uploads/fast-llm/v0.9/weights.zip - | sha256sum
# compare to RELEASES.md entry: 3b1f2e...
```

mike: RELEASES.md hash didn't match initially. re-downloaded, got same mismatch. reached out to upstream to confirm. tagging this in the manifests: unauthenticated-hash-mismatch.

anya: good catch. mark as HOLD until upstream confirms. add note in registry entry: provenance_status=unconfirmed, source_bucket=ext-uploads, observed_hash=..., claimed_hash=...

artifact-bot: new provisional artifact created: artifact_id=art-20260325-007, location=s3://redwood-staging/art-20260325-007/, status=provisional.

sara: tokenizer quick check results (local):
- vocab size: 50265 as claimed
- basic roundtrip: pass on most tokens, fails on a few unicode emojis (we should add fuzz tests)
- special tokens mapping looks inconsistent with README (cls vs bos).

anya: add tokenizer_issue tag and note to model-card: tokenizer_mismatch=true, token_edgecases=emoji, special_tokens_inconsistency.

david: quant plan: run baseline FP16 small-gen on 1GPU (nv=1, seq=128) to get baseline latency/perf, then run quant int8 per-channel and int4 group-wise, measure perplexity on eval-set-quick (2k tokens sample). if regression > 3% perplexity or visible artifacting -> fallback to int8-only.

mike: after upstream confirms, i'll GPG verify if they provide signed release. otherwise I'll produce sigstore attestation and upload manifest.json like:
```json
{
  "artifact_id": "art-20260325-007",
  "source": "s3://ext-uploads/fast-llm/v0.9/",
  "observed_hash": "3b1f2e...",
  "claimed_hash": "7c2a9d...",
  "provenance_status": "unconfirmed"
}
```

anya: good. note that registry requires flat model-card fields as strings. include: model_name, version, license, source_url, ingest_engineer, verification_status. i'll fill ingest_engineer=anya, verification_status=hold/unconfirmed.

sara: small FYI: tokenizer tokenization speed seems slower than our reference model by ~12% on the same CPU. might impact embed pipelines. add perf_note=tokenizer_slow.

david: will wait until artifact moves off HOLD before starting quant sweep; need final artifact path + manifest.

mike: upstream replied: they had a build step that altered packaging, new hashes in RELEASES.md v0.9.1. they published a signed tag (GPG) in their GitHub release. i'm pulling signed release now and verifying.

mike: verify commands I used:
```bash
curl -sL https://github.com/thirdparty/fast-llm/releases/download/v0.9.1/RELEASES.md -o RELEASES.md
sha256sum weights.zip  # compare
gpg --keyserver hkps://keys.openpgp.org --recv-keys 0xABCD1234
gpg --verify fast-llm-v0.9.1.tar.gz.sig fast-llm-v0.9.1.tar.gz
```

mike: GPG verified OK. updated artifact record and replaced provisional object with verified copy. artifact-bot: updated status.

artifact-bot: artifact_id=art-20260325-007 status=verified signed_by=0xABCD1234 manifest_uri=s3://redwood-model-registry/fast-llm/v0.9.1/manifest.json

anya: awesome. moving to registry and tagging for canary. next actions:
- sara: run tokenizer fuzz tests + publish results in thread (ticket eng-ml #4321)
- david: schedule quant sweep once manifest URI is final (use dedicated:small-quant pool)
- mike: upload model-card + signed manifest to registry path and set ACL to internal-read
- anya: create canary rollout with 1% traffic -> 10% over 24h if no regressions

sara: starting tokenizer fuzz run now, will post short results in ~45m.

david: prepping quant job, ETA 2h after start. will include per-layer breakdown and accuracy delta table.

anya: thanks team, keeping this thread as the single source for ingest notes. will update registry links when available. :white_check_mark:
